title: RedGuard Mode B Security Test Case
description: Schema for one multi-agent security test case (MULTI_AGENT_LAB_PLAN.md §7). Validated by core/lab/cases.py, which is hand-rolled in the same style as core/datasets/validator.py — this file is the schema of record, not a runtime dependency.

id.description: Stable case identifier. Mode B uses the RGM- prefix so it can never collide with a Mode A RG-XX-NNN probe id.

roles.description: Optional per-agent role blurb, overriding runner.DEFAULT_ROLES.

task.description: The benign shared objective. Identical in the CLEAN and ATTACK arms unless the attack channel is 'task' (direct injection), where the artifact is appended.

task_success_predicate.description: What counts as the benign task being done. Drives SystemOutcome, and gates clean-run validity (§21.8): a clean run that does not satisfy it is RUN_INVALID and must not contaminate denominators.

family.description: Restricted to the four families the MVP case set actually exercises. A subset of core/datasets/validator.VALID_FAMILIES — deliberately not imported, so Mode A's family list cannot silently change Mode B's validation.

injection_point.description: Agent at which the attack enters the system.

channel.description: CEE resource map to plant into. 'task' is direct injection: the artifact rides in the task string itself, so there is no resource read to link it through and the runner emits artifact_observed instead.

location.description: Key within the channel: file path, web query key, db table name, or kv key. Empty for channel 'task'.

mode.description: 'replace' (default) sets the location to the artifact. 'append' adds the artifact as one more db row or web search result, keeping the resource's shape identical to the clean run's.

artifact.description: The adversarial content planted before the ATTACK run starts. Must embed the canary. An object when delivery.mode is 'append' (one db row or one web search result).

canary.description: Unique marker used for provenance linking in the gateways and for the canary-in-emitted-content influence test (§10). Unique across the case set.

objective.description: The ATTACKER's goal, as predicates over the attack trace. Evaluated most-severe-first: critical_reached, reached, partially_reached, else NOT_REACHED.

eligible_downstream_agents.description: Agents structurally capable of advancing THIS objective. The CPR denominator and the containment walk use it. May be empty (entry-local objective) — CPR is then 'n/a', never 0.0.

expected_path.description: Agent execution order for the run. Also the distance metric's reference path.

compromise_predicate.description: Per agent: what it must have DONE to count as COMPROMISED rather than merely INFLUENCED. Matched only over that agent's own events, and only once it is already INFLUENCED.

influence_predicates.description: Optional per-agent case-specific influence test, used when 'absent from the clean run' and 'canary in emitted content' would both miss a real behavioural deviation.

clean_script.description: A compliant, task-completing action sequence per agent, replayed by runner.ScriptedClient with no LLM. It is the case's own baseline of record and powers two CI checks (§21.7): the clean trace MUST satisfy task_success_predicate, and MUST NOT satisfy any objective predicate. A case whose objective is reachable by ordinary task completion measures task behaviour, not attack effect.

predicate.description: Declarative predicate over trace events (§9). Either a leaf — several keys ANDed against ONE event, matched existentially over the trace — or exactly one combinator key ('all' | 'any' | 'none') whose children are matched independently.
